text: {"audited_lemma":"The fixed-word lift claim is essentially right, with directed-portal corrections, and it does not prove E(m,r)<=T(m,r). State (u,j), n=m+r. A generator changes u iff it is not one of: L at j=0 (j:=n-1), R at j=n-1 (j:=0), X at j<2 (j:=1-j). Thus non-identity zero-projection moves exist only on {0,1,n-1}, and only as the directed edges X:0↔1, L:0→n-1, R:n-1→0. There is no undirected edge 1—(n-1); that trip is the length-2 path X then L, or R then X. Every other mark is frozen: its only zero-projection block is empty. A shortest lift of a fixed V therefore uses, between projection letters and at the ends, a shortest path in this graph, hence block length 0, 1, or 2, never a longer detour. Legality is forced: projected L requires j≠0 and sends j to j-1; projected R requires j≠n-1 and sends j to j+1; projected X requires j≥2 and fixes j. Layered DP on (prefix index, mark) therefore computes the exact minimum lift length, or correctly reports that this fixed V has no lift, in O(n|V|) operations. Leading and trailing blocks must be included. All terminal marks j≥m are equivalent; do not privilege one root representative. Empty V with initial j in {2,...,m-1} is a genuine impossibility, since that mark is frozen and not terminal. None of this quantifies over sorting words, so it is not a proof of the conjecture.","constructive_subclass":"Free mark trajectory, including pure sweeps. Let ε(L)=-1, ε(R)=+1, ε(X)=0. Call (V,j) free if the positions p_0=j and p_i=p_{i-1}+ε(V_i) stay legal for every letter: V_i=L implies p_{i-1}≠0, V_i=R implies p_{i-1}≠n-1, V_i=X implies p_{i-1}≥2, and the final mark p_|V| lies in {0,1}∪{m,...,n-1}. Explicit nonempty patterns inside this class: (i) any j in {0,...,n-2} and V=R^{n-1-j}, which walks j,j+1,...,n-1 and ends terminal; (ii) any j in {1,...,n-1} and V=L^j, which walks j,...,0. These are structural conditions on V and j, not an assumption that a full sorting word is already known. They apply to sorting only when that V actually sorts the deleted-zero vector u.","proof":"Assume (V,j) is free and ell=|V|. Realize W as the pure concatenation of the letters of V, with no inserted block, and append a final portal only as below. Legality is exactly the condition that each letter changes u, and the induced action on u is the same-named generator, so the projection is exactly V. The mark updates by ε, so it follows p_i with overhead 0 during V. If p_ell≥m, stop; W is a lift to an allowed terminal mark and the routing overhead is 0. If p_ell=0, append one L: this is zero-projection, sends the mark to n-1≥m, and does not change u, so overhead becomes 1. If p_ell=1, append X then L: X swaps the mark with slot 0 and fixes u, then L sends 0 to n-1 and fixes u, so overhead becomes 2 and the terminal mark n-1 is allowed. No other final portal is required by the subclass. Thus overhead ≤2. Since m≥8, 2≤m-2. For the inductive slack, T(m,r)-T(m,r-1)=m-2, so the allowance Q+m-2-ell at ell≤Q+1 is at least m-3. Also m≥8 gives m-3≥5≥2, hence overhead ≤2≤Q+m-2-ell whenever a sorting word of length ≤Q+1 has some deletion index making (V,j) free. Pattern (i): each of the n-1-j letters R is applied at n-1-j distinct sites j,...,n-2, all different from n-1, so each projects; the mark ends at n-1≥m; overhead 0; ell=n-1-j≤m+r-1. Pattern (ii): each L is applied at j,...,1, all nonzero, so each projects; the mark ends at 0; the appended boundary L is zero-projection and overhead is exactly 1. In both patterns the inequality overhead≤m-2 is equality-free and does not depend on a finite sample. This does not show that every u, or every shortest word, has such a lift.","obstructions":"The portal graph is directed, so the undirected path slogan 1--0--(n-1) is false as an edge description; L cannot replace R on n-1→0. Frozen marks outside {0,1,n-1} cannot be corrected after the fact: a pure L^k from n-1 lands at n-1-k, and if that site lies in {2,...,m-1} the straight walk is the only zero-insertion-free walk and no terminalizing lift exists. Shortest-path blocks of length 2 are sometimes mandatory, not optional slack. Fixed-V optimality can return impossible and does not search over words; the already-proved projection identity |W|-S-I_z only audits a given full word. E(m,r-1)≤Q supplies some word of length ≤Q, not a free-trajectory word and not a word whose overhead meets Q+m-2-ell. The stated certificates already kill the stronger cap that every short smaller word lifts inside the old radius: no universal transfer from Q to T(m,r) follows. Phase repair by XL consumes one projected letter per overhead 1 and can be repeated; without a direction-change or free-trajectory hypothesis, overhead is not bounded by m-2. Base r=2 is not implied by any r-1 case.","next_test":"Do not treat computation as a proof. The open obligation is existential: for every full vector, some deleted zero must admit some sorting word V with ell≤Q+1 and a free trajectory, or a proved one-portal extension. Next structural target: one turn, V=R^a L^b or L^a R^b, whose monotonic phases hit the boundary at most once, with the single reset 0 -L→ n-1 or n-1 -R→ 0 charged explicitly and the landing residue checked against {0,1}∪{m,...,n-1}. Prove overhead ≤2 for every such one-turn word that sorts u, or exhibit a one-turn sorting word whose every deletion index is frozen outside the terminal set before the final letter. Separately, for r=2, a general argument is still required; the free-trajectory island does not cover it."}
